turn_text: The USDA has made a significant investment in the region's dairy industry. The department directed $20 million to the Dairy Business Innovation Alliance. U.S. Senator Tammy Baldwin authored the bill in creating these innovation programs. She explains why this additional money from USDA is important for Wisconsin's dairy industry.

First of all, we're headed to the end of June, but June is National Dairy Month, and so it made it a perfect occasion for Under Secretary Moffatt of the U.S. Department of Agriculture to come to Wisconsin and make this announcement about the investments we're making in our Made in Wisconsin economy. Back in 2018, I authored legislation to create the Dairy Business Innovation Initiative, and since that program's establishment, its footprint has grown very rapidly. Under Secretary Moffat came to Wisconsin to announce that an additional $80 million funded through the American Rescue Plan would be added nationally to the Dairy Business Innovation Initiative, including 20 million for the state of Wisconsin. Wonderful news to help our dairy businesses increase their processing capacity, do on-farm improvements and efficiencies, get technical assistance for projects and innovations, all sorts of things that they can do to make their operations more profitable.

You know, I really think it is a strong signal that nationally, there's a recognition that the Dairy Business Innovation Initiative is working. So, you know, it started up a few years back after my legislation was incorporated in the Farm Bill. And the first round of grants were smaller, but we've seen a real increase in the applications for grants and technical assistance. well in terms of on any particular announcement i usually here as they come out but i will tell you that we are hard at work right now on next fiscal years, add appropriations bills. Both the House and the Senate are working on ours. I chair the Senate Subcommittee on Agriculture. So we know shortly we'll be posting those publicly and hopefully we're going to keep some really solid support for the programs that are working really well. And we know that there still are some opportunities for pandemic related assistance, but I don't know of any immediate announcements that we should expect from the secretary.
Anything in the works in Congress? Are you watching anything come down the pipeline in terms of money for either dairy or agriculture that will benefit Wisconsin producers?

Oh, absolutely. So at the same time we're looking at the funding on the appropriation side, the Senate Ag Committee is working on the 2023 Farm Bill. We know that there will be a lot of support to continue programs that work well and are doing showing a strong record. There'll be things that will be tweaked and there'll probably be some new initiatives. But I do want to note one thing outside of the Farm Bill that may happen knock on wood this week is we've reached a bipartisan agreement on school nutrition waivers. What do I mean by that? I mean that during the pandemic, we waived some of the red tape and rules around the school nutrition programs. It allowed families that were struggling to be able to get food throughout the summer when school is out of session. And we know that the pandemic-related program is due to expire at the end of this month. And we hope to be able to renew it for the summer at minimum and hopefully beyond then. And you're confident in that bill? Well I'm confident that we have a bipartisan agreement worked out. What I am not confident about is whether every member will be in support of it but I think ultimately we will have that path and that will mean great things for students and their parents access to fresh nutritious food over the summer months when they're not getting breakfast or lunch in schools. And we know what a difference that those waivers made during the pandemic. And we're not quite out of the pandemic yet. So I think there's a good argument that these should last for a couple months to come.
